findings.description: The new regex trusts the first find root while swallowing additional roots. For `find ./build /etc -exec rm -rf {} \;`, it captures only the allow-listed `./build`, allowing the placeholder-only rm segment even though find also traverses /etc.
findings.failure_mode: The destructive-command guard permits deletion outside the allowed root. Previously, multiple roots cleared the inferred root and caused the ambiguous placeholder to be blocked.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore rejection of multiple roots, or parse and validate every find root before allowing placeholder deletion.

findings.description: Removing billing classification makes account-side 400 errors, including exhausted credit balance, terminal InvalidInputError exceptions. The same regression exists in _complete_nonstreaming.
findings.failure_mode: A valid completion request fails immediately when Anthropic credits are exhausted instead of falling through the configured provider chain to claude-headless.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve ProviderUnavailableError routing for billing-class errors in both transports while keeping request-validation errors terminal.

findings.description: Counting every completed sprint-* directory includes historical and sprint-bug-* directories, while total_sprints still counts only the current sprint.md plan. For a three-sprint plan with only sprint-1 completed, two unrelated completed directories make completed_sprints equal three.
findings.failure_mode: determine_state reports complete and suggests /deploy-production despite unfinished planned sprints.
findings.suggested_fix: Count completion markers only for sprint IDs belonging to the current plan or active cycle, using the same scope as total_sprints.

findings.description: The unquoted expansion splits find output on whitespace. If the project or configured grimoire directory contains spaces, each directory path becomes multiple loop entries and its COMPLETED marker is missed.
findings.failure_mode: Completed sprints are counted as zero, causing incorrect workflow state and progress for otherwise valid project paths.
findings.suggested_fix: Read directory names with a NUL-delimited loop using find -print0 and read -r -d '', keeping the counter in the current shell.

findings.description: Group 3 of `_re_find_exec_prefix` now captures only the FIRST token after `find` (`([^;&|)[:space:]]+)`) and `[^;&|)]*` swallows every other token up to `-exec`. The replaced loop at the old lines 803-811 counted root tokens and cleared `_seg_find_root` unless exactly one root was present. With `_seg_find_root="${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"` a multi-root invocation such as `find ./build /etc -exec rm -rf {} \;` resolves the root to `./build` only; `/etc` is never seen by the resolver.
findings.failure_mode: When the first root is allow-listed and the rm segment is placeholder-only (`{}`), the hook ALLOWS the command even though find also walks `/etc` (or any other second root) and rm -rf deletes under it. Base behavior cleared the root on count!=1 and fell to the per-arg ladder, which blocked `{}` as ambiguous. This is a safety-hook bypass for destructive deletes outside the allow-listed tree.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the single-token capture for the FIRST root but re-add a guard that rejects the prefix when a second non-flag path token follows it. Simplest: after the match, tokenize the swallowed span (`[^;&|)]*` can be captured as group 4) and clear `_seg_find_root` if any token before the first `-`/`!`/`(`/`\` token is a second path; or restore the removed counting loop over `BASH_REMATCH[3]`+span. Add a fixture: `find ./build /etc -exec rm -rf {} \;` must be BLOCKED.

findings.description: The new comment (lines 773-775) claims `find -L root -exec ...` 'keeps today's conservative behavior', but the new capture sets `_seg_find_root="-L"` (likewise `-name`, `!`, or `\(` for `find -name x -exec`, `find ! -name x -exec`, `find \( ... \) -exec`) instead of the empty string the old loop produced on `-*|'!'*|'('*|'\'*`. Downstream code that previously branched on an empty root now receives a flag token as a path.
findings.failure_mode: Behavior for flag-first find invocations is now whatever the root-resolution code does with a non-path string, not the documented 'conservative' fallback. If any resolver step does `realpath`/`cd`/prefix matching on `-L`, the result is undefined relative to the comment and untested.
findings.suggested_fix: Either exclude leading-dash/`!`/`(`/`\` tokens from group 3 (e.g. `([^-;&|)[:space:]!(\\][^;&|)[:space:]]*)`) so the regex fails to match and the old empty-root path is taken, or explicitly clear `_seg_find_root` when it starts with `-`, `!`, `(`, or `\`. Add a fixture for `find -L ./root -exec rm -rf {} \;`.

findings.description: Both the streaming path (lines 139-141) and the non-streaming path (`_complete_nonstreaming`, lines 221-223) now raise `InvalidInputError` for every non-429, non-5xx status. The removed `_is_billing_class_error` routing sent account-side 400s (credit balance, quota_exceeded, invoice_overdue, billing_disabled, payment_required, insufficient_quota) to `ProviderUnavailableError` so the retry layer chain-walks to the next provider (cycle-109 #883 Bug 3). That fix is silently reverted.
findings.failure_mode: When the Anthropic API key hits a billing/quota condition, the adapter raises a terminal, non-retryable `InvalidInputError`. The retry layer treats it as a request-shape problem and never fails over to `claude-headless`, so every call in the pipeline fails hard instead of degrading to the fallback provider. This is a production-availability regression of a previously fixed bug.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore `_BILLING_CLASS_TOKENS` / `_is_billing_class_error` and the `ProviderUnavailableError` branch in both `_complete_streaming` and `_complete_nonstreaming` (or move the classifier into `base.py` if the goal was deduplication). If the removal is intentional, the SDD/known-failures doc for #883 must be updated and the retry layer must gain an equivalent classifier before this can merge.

findings.cross_file_justification: `.claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_adapter_billing_class.py` (untouched by this PR) does `from loa_cheval.providers.anthropic_adapter import _is_billing_class_error` and asserts `ProviderUnavailableError` for billing-class 400s. The symbol is deleted in this diff.
findings.description: The diff deletes the module-level `_BILLING_CLASS_TOKENS` and `_is_billing_class_error` without touching the test module that imports them. Reviewer verified 9 of 12 tests in that file fail against head.
findings.failure_mode: Test suite fails on import/collection or on behavioral asserts; CI for the adapters package goes red on merge and masks any other regressions in the same run.
findings.suggested_fix: Either restore the symbol (preferred, see DISS-003) or update/delete `test_anthropic_adapter_billing_class.py` in the same PR with a documented rationale. Never remove a classifier that has dedicated regression tests without touching those tests.

findings.description: `get_completed_sprints` now counts every `a2a/sprint-*` directory containing a `COMPLETED` marker instead of iterating `sprint-1..get_total_sprints()`. The `-name "sprint-*"` glob also matches `sprint-bug-*` directories and any stale directories from earlier cycles that were not archived. `determine_state` (line ~148) does `completed >= total && total > 0 => STATE_COMPLETE`, and `main` iterates only `sprint-1..total` for current-sprint detection, so the two functions now disagree on which directories count.
findings.failure_mode: With a2a containing sprint-1..5 COMPLETED (stale), sprint-6 open, sprint-bug-1 COMPLETED and a sprint.md declaring 3 sprints, head reports 6/3 and state `complete`, suggesting `/deploy-production` while a sprint is still in progress. Reviewer reproduced this (base 3/3, head 6/3). JSON `completed_sprints` also exceeds `total_sprints`, breaking any consumer that assumes completed<=total.
findings.suggested_fix: Bound the count to the sprints in the plan: keep the base `for ((i=1; i<=total; i++))` loop over `${a2a_dir}/sprint-${i}/COMPLETED`, or if the intent is to honor ledger `global_id`s, iterate the active cycle's sprint ids from the ledger rather than globbing the filesystem. At minimum exclude `sprint-bug-*` and cap at `total`.

findings.description: `for dir in ${sprint_dirs}` word-splits the find output on IFS whitespace and applies pathname expansion. `_GRIMOIRE_DIR` is a user path; any space in it (common on macOS, e.g. `~/My Projects/...`) splits every directory into fragments that do not exist. The base code used the quoted `"${a2a_dir}/sprint-${i}/COMPLETED"` and was space-safe.
findings.failure_mode: Count is 0 for every project whose grimoire path contains whitespace, so `STATE_COMPLETE` can never be reached and progress/`completed_sprints` in the JSON are wrong. Reviewer reproduced 0/3 on a path with a space. Under `set -u`/`pipefail` nothing errors, so the wrong value is silently cached by `store_cache`.
findings.suggested_fix: Avoid word-splitting: `for dir in "${a2a_dir}"/sprint-*/; do [[ -d "$dir" ]] || continue; ...` with `shopt -s nullglob`, or `while IFS= read -r -d '' dir; do ...; done < <(find "${a2a_dir}" -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'sprint-*' -print0)`.

findings.description: All three behavioral changes (find-root capture semantics, 4xx error-class routing, completed-sprint counting) ship with no new or updated fixtures/tests, and `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md` has no `## AC Verification` section. The safety hook in particular is fixture-driven and the comment explicitly declares a 'documented gap' without a fixture pinning it.
findings.failure_mode: Regressions in DISS-001/002/005/006 are undetectable by the existing suite; the only test file that did cover one of the changes (billing-class) now fails.
findings.suggested_fix: Add hook fixtures for multi-root and flag-first `find -exec rm` forms; add a bats/shell test for `get_completed_sprints` with stale and space-containing paths; update or restore the billing-class tests; fill in AC Verification in reviewer.md.
